source.title: Stress-Aware Resilient Neural Training
source.authors: Ashkan Shakarami; Yousef Yeganeh; Azade Farshad; Lorenzo Nicolè; Stefano Ghidoni; N. Navab

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no evident cutoff or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a stress-aware training intervention changes generalization-related outcomes in vision models and datasets, a new method and setting relative to the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for its own SAL training method. Results cited from other studies, stress values used to trigger interventions, and figure-only geometry claims without stated numeric outcomes are not separate result rows.
record.test_reason: SAL uses the premise that flatter minima improve generalization to motivate a training intervention and reports its own performance. None of V1–V8 is tested: optimizer comparisons include no SGD, dropout is held fixed, and gradient norms and landscape visualizations do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its association with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that accumulated training stress triggers noise or stronger parameter shifts, improving generalization and stability, especially under unstable conditions. These are their conclusions; the paper leaves multiple-run significance testing and component ablations to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a stress-triggered noise and final-layer weight deformation procedure to conventional training; uses a pre-trained DenseNet201 backbone for its primary stable setup. The intervention and outcomes are not those in the listed original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across architecture, dataset, optimizer, and training regime; the paper describes stronger benefits under unstable conditions. It reports a Top-5 accuracy decrease for DenseNet121 and MobileNetV2 in Table 1 despite Top-1 improvements. The optimizer-specific baseline comparisons are incomplete.

fits_no_version.finding: SAL raises Top-1 accuracy across five Imagenette architectures, while Top-5 accuracy decreases for DenseNet121 and MobileNetV2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stress-triggered training interventions can improve reported vision accuracy, with effects depending on architecture and metric.

fits_no_version.finding: SAL raises reported Top-1 accuracy across seven datasets; gains range from 0.06 percentage points on Tiny-ImageNet to 1.50 on Corel-1k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAL improves reported benchmark accuracy across the tested datasets, with varying gain sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: SAL optimizer configurations achieve 87.59–89.17% Top-1 accuracy versus 86.98% for baseline Adam; matched non-SAL baselines for the other optimizers are absent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAL configurations using several adaptive optimizers outperform the reported baseline Adam configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors describe gradient-norm reductions after plastic interventions and stress increases during loss stagnation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAL interventions coincide with changes in training gradient norms and its internally defined stress signal.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report improved validation accuracy and recovery from instability for ResNet50V2 on Corel-1k under degraded training conditions; numerical outcomes are not supplied in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAL can improve training stability and validation performance in the tested degraded setup.

record.problems: No multiple-run statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; the authors identify these as future work. No ablation isolates stress accumulation, noise injection, and plastic deformation. Several claims about degraded-condition accuracy and geometry rely on figures without numeric outcomes in the text. Optimizer comparison lacks matched baseline results for Adamax, Nadam, and RMSProp.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted additional repeated metrics and resource-use measures (training time, memory, inference time) from Tables 1–3, plus Top-5 results for the seven-dataset sweep and class-level metrics in Table 5; these do not map to the versions and were not needed to preserve version coverage. Table 4 resolution sweep has no paired baseline values, so does not report a treatment effect.

untested.parts: No matched natural-label and random-label training or held-out comparison.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or manipulation of local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison under limited or broader tuning.
No batch-size comparison or test of remedies for a large-batch penalty.
Dropout rate is fixed at 0.5 in the primary setup; no dropout ablation or removal comparison.
No magnitude-aware perturbation-tolerance measure, ranking of generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No identification and removal of highly memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T3 classification is incorrect because a new generalization-related intervention does not itself test any specified version. All rows remain unlinked, and no version verdict is warranted. Method-performance comparisons should be retained as findings outside the versions rather than claim-testing evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train the same architectures and recipes on natural versus random labels.
No width sweep or test error analysis around the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks or local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD; its optimizer comparison evaluates SAL-enhanced methods against a baseline Adam result.
Dropout is present in the architecture, but the paper does not compare dropout settings or its removal.
Reports sharpness-related claims but does not test magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or compare generalization-gap rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.
